```{r}
#| warning: false
create_overview_cards <- function(data) {
  # Calculate key statistics using adjusted values
  total_movies <- nrow(data)
  total_revenue <- sum(data$BoxOffice_adjusted, na.rm = TRUE) # Using adjusted
  avg_rating <- mean(data$imdbRating, na.rm = TRUE)
  date_range <- paste(
    min(data$Released_year, na.rm = TRUE),
    "-",
    max(data$Released_year, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

  # Extract unique counts
  all_directors <- unlist(str_split(data$Director, ", "))
  unique_directors <- n_distinct(all_directors[!is.na(all_directors)])

  all_genres <- unlist(str_split(data$Genre, ", "))
  unique_genres <- n_distinct(all_genres[!is.na(all_genres)])

  # Return as list for display
  list(
    total_movies = total_movies,
    total_revenue = dollar(total_revenue),
    avg_rating = round(avg_rating, 2),
    date_range = date_range,
    unique_directors = (unique_directors),
    unique_genres = unique_genres
  )
}

cards <- create_overview_cards(movies_clean)
```

```{r}
# | title: "Genre Universe: Box Office Dominance (Inflation-Adjusted)"
create_genre_treemap <- function(data) {
  genre_stats <- data %>%
    separate_rows(Genre, sep = ", ") %>%
    group_by(Genre) %>%
    summarise(
      total_revenue = sum(BoxOffice_adjusted, na.rm = TRUE), # Using adjusted
      movie_count = n(),
      avg_rating = mean(imdbRating, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(movie_count >= 10) %>%
    mutate(
      label = paste(
        Genre,
        "\n",
        "$",
        round(total_revenue / 1e9, 1),
        "B\n",
        movie_count,
        " movies\n",
        "★",
        round(avg_rating, 1)
      )
    )

  ggplot(
    genre_stats,
    aes(area = total_revenue, fill = avg_rating, label = label)
  ) +
    geom_treemap() +
    geom_treemap_text(colour = "white", place = "centre", size = 12) +
    scale_fill_viridis(name = "Avg Rating", option = "plasma") +
    labs(
      subtitle = "Size = Total Revenue (2024 dollars) | Color = Average Rating"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

```{r}
genre_treemap
```

```{r}
create_data_table <- function(data) {
  # Prepare table data with both nominal and adjusted values
  table_data <- data %>%
    select(
      Title,
      Released_year,
      Genre,
      Rated,
      Director,
      BoxOffice_num,
      BoxOffice_adjusted,
      Metascore,
      imdbRating,
      imdbVotes,
      Runtime_num
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Format nominal box office
      BoxOffice_Nominal = case_when(
        is.na(BoxOffice_num) ~ "N/A",
        BoxOffice_num == 0 ~ "N/A",
        BoxOffice_num < 1000000 ~ paste0(
          "$",
          format(round(BoxOffice_num / 1000), big.mark = ","),
          "K"
        ),
        BoxOffice_num < 1000000000 ~ paste0(
          "$",
          format(round(BoxOffice_num / 1000000, 1), big.mark = ","),
          "M"
        ),
        TRUE ~ paste0(
          "$",
          format(round(BoxOffice_num / 1000000000, 2), big.mark = ","),
          "B"
        )
      ),
      # Format adjusted box office
      BoxOffice_Adj = case_when(
        is.na(BoxOffice_adjusted) ~ "N/A",
        BoxOffice_adjusted == 0 ~ "N/A",
        BoxOffice_adjusted < 1000000 ~ paste0(
          "$",
          format(round(BoxOffice_adjusted / 1000), big.mark = ","),
          "K"
        ),
        BoxOffice_adjusted < 1000000000 ~ paste0(
          "$",
          format(round(BoxOffice_adjusted / 1000000, 1), big.mark = ","),
          "M"
        ),
        TRUE ~ paste0(
          "$",
          format(round(BoxOffice_adjusted / 1000000000, 2), big.mark = ","),
          "B"
        )
      ),
      # Format rating
      IMDb_Rating = round(imdbRating, 1),
      # Format other columns
      Votes = format(imdbVotes, big.mark = ","),
      Runtime = paste(Runtime_num, "min")
    ) %>%
    select(
      Title,
      Released_year,
      Genre,
      Rated,
      Director,
      BoxOffice_Nominal,
      BoxOffice_Adj,
      Metascore,
      IMDb_Rating,
      Votes,
      Runtime
    )

  # Create data table
  datatable(
    table_data,
    filter = 'top',
    rownames = FALSE,
    options = list(
      pageLength = 25,
      searchHighlight = TRUE,
      paging = TRUE,
      dom = 'Bfrtip',
      buttons = c('copy', 'csv', 'excel'),
      columnDefs = list(
        list(className = 'dt-center', targets = c(1, 6, 7, 8, 9)),
        list(className = 'dt-right', targets = c(4, 5))
      )
    ),
    colnames = c(
      'Title',
      'Year',
      'Genres',
      'Rated',
      'Director(s)',
      'Box Office (Nominal)',
      'Box Office (2024 adj.)',
      'Metascore',
      'IMDb Rating',
      'Votes',
      'Runtime'
    )
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| title: "Interactive Movie Explorer 2000-2025"
movies_table <- create_data_table(movies_clean)
movies_table
```

# Genre Analysis 

## Row

```{r}
create_genre_combinations <- function(data) {
  genre_combos <- data %>%
    filter(str_detect(Genre, ", ")) %>%
    mutate(
      genre_count = str_count(Genre, ", ") + 1,
      primary_genre = str_split(Genre, ", ", simplify = TRUE)[, 1],
      secondary_genre = str_split(Genre, ", ", simplify = TRUE)[, 2]
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(secondary_genre), secondary_genre != "") %>%
    group_by(primary_genre, secondary_genre) %>%
    summarise(
      count = n(),
      avg_revenue = mean(BoxOffice_adjusted, na.rm = TRUE), # Using adjusted
      avg_rating = mean(imdbRating, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(count >= 5)

  heatmap <- ggplot(genre_combos, aes(x = primary_genre, y = secondary_genre)) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = avg_revenue / 1e6)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(avg_rating, 1)), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_viridis(name = "Avg Revenue\n(2024 Million $)") +
    labs(
      subtitle = "Color = Average Revenue (2024 dollars) | Numbers = Average Rating",
      x = "Primary Genre",
      y = "Secondary Genre"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "lines"),
      plot.caption.position = "panel",
      legend.spacing.y = unit(0.2, "lines"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 8)
    )

  return(heatmap)
}
```

```{r}
create_seasonal_analysis <- function(data) {
  seasonal_data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(Released)) %>%
    mutate(
      month = month(Released, label = TRUE),
      week = week(Released),
      quarter = quarter(Released)
    ) %>%
    group_by(month) %>%
    summarise(
      avg_revenue = mean(BoxOffice_adjusted, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6, # Using adjusted
      movie_count = n(),
      avg_rating = mean(imdbRating, na.rm = TRUE),
      blockbuster_pct = sum(BoxOffice_adjusted > 500000000, na.rm = TRUE) /
        n() *
        100, # Adjusted threshold
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  polar_plot <- seasonal_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = month)) +
    geom_col(aes(y = avg_revenue, fill = avg_rating), width = 0.9) +
    geom_text(aes(y = avg_revenue + 5, label = movie_count), size = 3) +
    coord_polar() +
    scale_fill_viridis(name = "Avg Rating") +
    labs(
      subtitle = "Bar height = Average Revenue (2024 dollars) | Numbers = Movie Count",
      x = "",
      y = "Average Revenue (Million USD)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())

  return(polar_plot)
}
```

```{r}
# 4. BOX OFFICE DISTRIBUTION - Show both nominal and adjusted
create_box_office_distribution <- function(data) {
  # Adjusted distribution
  p1 <- data %>%
    filter(BoxOffice_adjusted > 0) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = BoxOffice_adjusted / 1e6)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_x_log10(
      breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000),
      labels = c("0.1", "1", "10", "100", "1K", "10K")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Box Office Distribution - Inflation Adjusted (2024 dollars)",
      x = "Box Office (Million USD)",
      y = "Number of Movies"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
  return(p1)
}

```

```{r}
log_dist <- create_box_office_distribution(movies_clean)
log_dist
```

# Top performance
## Row {height="50%"}

```{r}

create_top_performers <- function(data) {

  # ensure Released_year is numeric and filter
  data <- data %>%
    mutate(Year_num = as.numeric(Released_year)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Year_num),
           Year_num >= 2000,
           Year_num <= 2025)

  # Revenue – lollipop with dropdown by Year

  top_revenue_by_year <- data %>%
    group_by(Year = Year_num) %>%
    arrange(desc(BoxOffice_adjusted), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    slice_head(n = 20) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(BoxOffice_m = BoxOffice_adjusted / 1e6)

  years_rev <- sort(unique(top_revenue_by_year$Year))
  n_rev_years <- length(years_rev)

  revenue_dropdown <- plot_ly()
  buttons_rev <- list()

  for (i in seq_along(years_rev)) {
    yr <- years_rev[i]

    df <- top_revenue_by_year %>%
      filter(Year == yr) %>%
      arrange(BoxOffice_m, Title) %>%
      distinct(Title, .keep_all = TRUE)

    df$Title <- factor(df$Title, levels = df$Title)

    revenue_dropdown <- revenue_dropdown %>%
      add_segments(
        data = df,
        x = 0, xend = ~BoxOffice_m,
        y = ~Title, yend = ~Title,
        showlegend = FALSE,
        line = list(color = "gray70", width = 1),
        visible = if (i == 1) TRUE else FALSE
      ) %>%
      add_markers(
        data = df,
        x = ~BoxOffice_m,
        y = ~Title,
        showlegend = FALSE,
        marker = list(
          size = 8,
          color = ~imdbRating,
          colorscale = "Viridis",
          showscale = (i == 1),
          colorbar = list(
            title = "IMDb Rating",
            x = 1.10,          ## <<< push colorbar to the far right
            y = 0.5
          ),
          line = list(color = "white", width = 0.5)
        ),
        name = yr,
        visible = if (i == 1) TRUE else FALSE,
        hovertemplate = paste(
          "<b>%{y}</b><br>",
          "Box Office: %{x:.1f} M<br>",
          "IMDb: %{marker.color}<extra></extra>"
        )
      )

    vis_vec <- rep(FALSE, 2 * n_rev_years)
    vis_vec[(2 * i - 1):(2 * i)] <- TRUE

    buttons_rev[[i]] <- list(
      method = "update",
      args = list(
        list(visible = vis_vec),
        list(
          title = paste0(
            "Top 20 Movies by Box Office Revenue (Inflation-Adjusted) – ",
            yr,
            "<br><sup>All values in 2024 dollars</sup>"
          )
        )
      ),
      label = as.character(yr)
    )
  }

  revenue_dropdown <- revenue_dropdown %>%
    layout(
      title = list(
        text = "Top 20 Movies by Box Office Revenue (Inflation-Adjusted)<br><sup>All values in 2024 dollars</sup>",
        x = 0.5,
        xanchor = "center"
      ),
      xaxis = list(
        title = "Box Office (Million USD)",
        zeroline = FALSE
      ),
      yaxis = list(
        title = "",
        showgrid = FALSE
      ),
      margin = list(l = 140, r = 80, t = 80, b = 60),  ## <<< a bit more right margin
      paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
      plot_bgcolor  = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
      updatemenus = list(
        list(
          type = "dropdown",
          x = 0.02, y = 1.15,          ## <<< keep dropdown in top-left
          xanchor = "left",
          yanchor = "top",
          buttons = buttons_rev,
          direction = "down",
          showactive = TRUE
        )
      )
    )

  # Rating – horizontal bar chart with dropdown by Year

  top_rated_by_year <- data %>%
    filter(imdbVotes > 50000) %>%
    group_by(Year = Year_num) %>%
    arrange(desc(imdbRating), desc(imdbVotes), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    slice_head(n = 20) %>%
    ungroup()

  years_rat <- sort(unique(top_rated_by_year$Year))
  n_rat_years <- length(years_rat)

  rating_dropdown <- plot_ly()
  buttons_rat <- list()

  for (i in seq_along(years_rat)) {
    yr <- years_rat[i]

    df <- top_rated_by_year %>%
      filter(Year == yr) %>%
      arrange(imdbRating, Title) %>%
      distinct(Title, .keep_all = TRUE)

    df$Title <- factor(df$Title, levels = df$Title)

    rating_dropdown <- rating_dropdown %>%
      add_trace(
        data = df,
        type = "bar",
        orientation = "h",
        x = ~imdbRating,
        y = ~Title,
        text = ~paste0("Votes: ", comma(imdbVotes)),
        textposition = "outside",
        marker = list(
          color = ~log10(imdbVotes),
          colorscale = "Viridis",
          showscale = (i == 1),
          colorbar = list(
            title = "Votes (log10)",
            x = 1.10,      ## <<< move this colorbar right too
            y = 0.5
          )
        ),
        name = yr,
        visible = if (i == 1) TRUE else FALSE,
        hovertemplate = paste(
          "<b>%{y}</b><br>",
          "IMDb: %{x}<br>",
          "%{text}<extra></extra>"
        )
      )

    vis_vec <- rep(FALSE, n_rat_years)
    vis_vec[i] <- TRUE

    buttons_rat[[i]] <- list(
      method = "update",
      args = list(
        list(visible = vis_vec),
        list(
          title = paste0("Top 20 Highest Rated Movies – ", yr)
        )
      ),
      label = as.character(yr)
    )
  }

  rating_dropdown <- rating_dropdown %>%
    layout(
      title = list(
        text = "Top 20 Highest Rated Movies",
        x = 0.5,
        xanchor = "center"
      ),
      xaxis = list(
        title = "IMDb Rating",
        zeroline = FALSE
      ),
      yaxis = list(
        title = "",
        showgrid = FALSE
      ),
      showlegend = FALSE,
      margin = list(l = 180, r = 80, t = 80, b = 60),  ## <<< more right margin
      paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
      plot_bgcolor  = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
      updatemenus = list(
        list(
          type = "dropdown",
          x = 0.02, y = 1.15,          ## <<< same top-left position
          xanchor = "left",
          yanchor = "top",
          buttons = buttons_rat,
          direction = "down",
          showactive = TRUE
        )
      )
    )

  list(
    revenue = revenue_dropdown,
    rating  = rating_dropdown
  )
}

```
